([[Orlando, Florida]]) | college = [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]] (2018–2020) | draft_year = 2020 | career_start = 2021 | career_end = | years1 = [[2020–21 NBA G League season|2021]] | team1 = [[Agua Caliente Clippers]] | years2 = 2021 | team2 = Hapoel Acre | years3 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team3 = Agua Caliente Clippers | years4 = 2022 | team4 = [[Fraser Valley Bandits]] | years5 = 2022 | team5 = [[Napoli Basket (2016)|GeVi Napoli]] | years6 = [[2022-23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team6 = [[Ontario Clippers]] | years7 = 2023 | team7 = [[Metros de Santiago]] | years8 = 2023 | team8 = [[Piratas de La Guaira]] | years9 = 2023–2024 | team9 = [[Real Estelí Baloncesto|Real Estelí]] | years10 = 2024–present | team10 = [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]] | highlights = }} '''Emmitt Mack Williams V''' (born September 15, 1998) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU Tigers]]. ==High school career== As a freshman, Williams played for [[Lehigh Senior High School]] in [[Lehigh Acres, Florida]], where he averaged 15.3 points and 11.2 rebounds per game before transferring to [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]], for his sophomore season.{{cite web |last1=Mull |first1=Cory |title=Top basketball prospect leaves Lehigh |url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/2015/10/06/lehigh-sophomore-emmitt-williams-top-25-prospect-withdraws-from-lehigh-before-city-of-palms-press-conference/73411208/ |website=[[The News-Press]] |accessdate=February 1, 2020 |date=October 6, 2015}} At IMG Academy, he was teammates with highly touted recruits [[Trevon Duval]] and [[Silvio De Sousa]] and played for one of the best teams in the country.{{cite web |last1=Collings |first1=Buddy |title=Emmitt Williams joins loaded Oak Ridge basketball |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/os-hs-sp-emmitt-williams-oak-ridge-0816-story.html |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |accessdate=February 1, 2020 |date=August 15, 2017}} In the 2015–16 season, Williams averaged 16.4 points, 12.6 rebounds and 2.9 blocks per game, playing in the [[Power forward (basketball)|power forward]] position.{{Cite news|url=https://eu.news-press.com/story/sports/2016/06/09/emmitt-williams-developing-his-hoop-skill-img-academy/85566716/|title=Emmitt Williams developing his hoop skill at IMG Academy|author=Mull, Cory|newspaper=[[The News-Press]]|date=June 9, 2016|access-date=February 3, 2020}} For his senior season, Williams transferred to [[Oak Ridge High School (Orlando, Florida)|Oak Ridge High School]] in [[Orlando, Florida]]. On October 11, 2017, he was arrested on charges of [[felony|felonious]] [[sexual battery]] and [[false imprisonment]].{{cite web |last1=Regan |first1=Adam |last2=Soffian |first2=Seth |title=Former Lehigh hoops star Emmitt Williams arrested |url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/10/18/former-lehigh-hoops-star-emmitt-williams-arrested-charged-felony-sexual-battery-orlando/775758001/ |website=[[The News-Press]] |accessdate=January 31, 2020 |date=October 18, 2017}} Williams pleaded not guilty and was released on $13,500 bond six days later.{{cite web |last1=Soffian |first1=Seth |title=Emmitt Williams back on court 5 weeks after rape arrest |url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/2017/12/04/star-basketball-recruit-emmitt-williams-back-court-orlando-oak-ridge-hig-rape-charges-still-not-file/919643001/ |website=[[The News-Press]] |accessdate=January 31, 2020 |date=December 4, 2017}} He made his debut for Oak Ridge on December 1, after sitting out his first two games. On December 20, his charges were dismissed after the case was deemed "not suitable for prosecution."{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Felony charges against 5-star recruit Emmitt Williams are dismissed |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/21849069/five-star-recruit-emmitt-williams-felony-sexual-battery-false-imprisonment-charges-dismissed |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=February 1, 2020 |date=December 22, 2017}} Williams averaged 17.6 points, 12.4 rebounds and 1.7 blocks per game, leading his team to the [[Florida High School Athletic Association]] (FHSAA) Class 9A state championship.{{cite web |last1=Jacquez |first1=Joe |title=Emmitt Williams: 4 things to know about the LSU basketball forward |url=https://www.theadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/lsu/2019/12/14/emmitt-williams-lsu-basketball-tigers-stats-jordan-classic/4349376002/ |website=[[The Daily Advertiser (Lafayette, Louisiana)|The Daily Advertiser]] |accessdate=February 1, 2020 |date=December 14, 2019}} On April 8, 2018, he recorded 44 points, seven rebounds and three steals at the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and was named [[most valuable player]] (MVP) of the game. He broke the single-game scoring record for the event previously held by [[LeBron James]].{{cite web |last1=Squadron |first1=Alex |title=Emmitt Williams Breaks LeBron's Record With 44 Points At Jordan Brand Classic |url=https://www.slamonline.com/slam-tv/emmit-williams-breaks-lebrons-record-44-points-2018-jordan-brand-classic/ |website=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]] |accessdate=January 31, 2020 |date=April 9, 2018}} He also took part in the [[Ballislife All-American Game]], of which he was named co-MVP with [[Moses Brown (basketball)|Moses Brown]] after he was the game's top scorer (31 points) and best rebounder (12).{{Cite web|url=http://www.ballislifeallamerican.com/the-history/records/|title=All-Time Box Scores|website=ballislifeallamerican.com|access-date=February 3, 2020}}{{cite news|title=McClung wins slam dunk contest and scores 20 in all-star game|date=May 6, 2018|newspaper=Bristol Herald Courier|url=https://www.heraldcourier.com/sports/mcclung-wins-slam-dunk-contest-and-scores-in-all-star/article_2c3e59e6-50e3-11e8-b814-2f28e0b4b69a.html}} ===Recruiting=== Williams was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the most highly rated [[power forward (basketball)|power forwards]] in the 2018 recruiting class. On January 26, 2018, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]] over offers from [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]] and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], among others.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Five-star forward Emmitt Williams commits to LSU |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/22222821/five-star-forward-emmitt-williams-oak-ridge-high-school-florida-commits-lsu |publisher=[[ESPN]] |accessdate=February 1, 2020 |date=January 26, 2018}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Emmitt Williams | position = [[Power forward (basketball)|PF]] | hometown = [[Fort Myers, Florida|Fort Myers, FL]] | highschool = [[Oak Ridge High School (Orlando, Florida)|Oak Ridge]] (FL) | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 215 | 40 = | commitdate = January 26, 2018 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 91 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2018 | rivals ref title = LSU 2018 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2018 LSU Tigers Recruiting Class | rivals school = lsu | scout s = | espn schoolid = 99 | 247 overall = 31 | rivals overall = 23 | espn overall = 21 | accessdate = February 1, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== As a freshman, Williams averaged 7.0 points and 5.4 rebounds per game, making eight starts on a team that reached the Sweet 16. He had a season-high 15 points twice. Williams scored 13 points and a career-best 14 rebounds in a 79–78 overtime win at [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]]. Following the season, he declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] but decided to return.{{cite news |last1=Mickles |first1=Sheldon |title=Emmitt Williams will return to LSU basketball program; forward is latest to return |url=https://www.theadvocate.com/baton_rouge/sports/lsu/article_53687128-7e46-11e9-9595-eb1b62217ac2.html |accessdate=February 2, 2020 |work=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]] |date=May 28, 2019}} On November 24, 2019, Williams scored a career-high 27 points and collected nine rebounds in a 96–83 win against [[Rhode Island Rams men's basketball|Rhode Island]].{{cite news |title=Williams has career-high 27 in LSU's win over Rhode Island |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169855 |accessdate=February 2, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] 6.6 rebounds, and 1.2 blocks per game.{{cite web |last1=Welser |first1=Joel |title=LSU Tigers |url=https://www.collegesportsmadness.com/article/18449 |website=College Sports Madness |accessdate=March 23, 2020}} Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |title=LSU's Emmitt Williams headed into NBA draft pool after two seasons with the Tigers Williams used Strawder's death as motivation to continue playing basketball.{{cite web |last1=Belman |first1=Jarred |title=Emmitt Williams hopes to carry on his "brother's" legacy |url=https://theleftbench.com/blog/2016/10/03/emmitt-williams-hopes-carry-brothers-legacy/ |website=The Left Bench |accessdate=February 1, 2020 |date=October 3, 2016}} Currently, Williams is signed with NBA Agent, Michael Raymond of Raymond Representation and is Managed by Jonathan Moore at CK Talent Management. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[https://lsusports.net/sports/mens-basketball/roster/emmitt-williams/5503 LSU Tigers bio] *[https://web.archive.org/web/20210514221843/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/w/williams-emmitt.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{Jordan Brand Classic All-American Boys Game MVP}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Williams, Emmitt}} [[Category:1998 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Agua Caliente Clippers players]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Canada]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Israel]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Italy]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Nicaragua]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in the Dominican Republic]] [[Category:American expatriate basketball people in Venezuela]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Florida]] [[Category:Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball) players]] [[Category:LSU Tigers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Metros de Santiago players]] [[Category:Napoli Basket (2016) players]] [[Category:Ontario Clippers players]] [[Category:Power forwards]] [[Category:Real Estelí Baloncesto players]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Fort Myers, Florida]] [[Category:Vancouver Bandits players]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]]
